plainExplanation: NSAIDs reduce blood flow directly into the kidney filtering units (glomeruli). Even short courses or over-the-counter gels can cause acute kidney injury or worsen existing CKD.
actionToTake: Avoid NSAIDs unless specifically prescribed by your kidney specialist. For mild pain, ask your pharmacist if paracetamol is suitable for you.
reviewedBy: Dr. R. Sharma (Consultant Nephrologist) & E. Davies (Lead Renal Pharmacist)

plainExplanation: When you have severe vomiting, diarrhea, or a high fever, you lose fluid quickly. Taking these medicines while dehydrated can cause your blood pressure or kidney function to drop sharply.
actionToTake: Ask your GP or kidney team about your personal 'Sick-Day Rules'. If you become unwell with vomiting or diarrhea, contact your team to check if you should pause them temporarily.

plainExplanation: Low-sodium salt alternatives replace sodium with high levels of potassium. When kidneys filter more slowly, excess potassium can build up in the blood (hyperkalaemia), which can affect heart rhythm.
actionToTake: Do not use potassium-based salt substitutes without explicit approval from your renal dietitian or doctor. Flavour food with herbs, spices, lemon juice, or garlic instead.
reviewedBy: E. Davies (Lead Renal Pharmacist) & S. Patel (Specialist Renal Dietitian)

examples: High-dose Vitamin C / Cranberry concentrated extracts
plainExplanation: Herbal remedies are not regulated as strictly as medicines and may contain heavy metals, potassium, or compounds that directly injure the kidneys or interact with kidney medications.
actionToTake: Always bring a complete list of any herbal pills, powders, or supplements to your pharmacist or kidney clinic before starting them.

plainExplanation: Some specialized hospital scans use dye injections to highlight blood vessels. In reduced kidney function, adequate hydration before and after the scan protects the kidneys.
actionToTake: Always tell the imaging radiographer and doctor that you have kidney disease and have your latest eGFR reading available.

plainExplanation: These medications offer strong kidney and heart protection. However, GLP-1 medicines can cause nausea and reduced fluid intake, while SGLT2 inhibitors increase urine output. Staying hydrated is vital.
actionToTake: Drink enough water throughout the day. If you develop persistent vomiting or cannot keep fluids down, contact your prescriber or pharmacist promptly.
